newsitem.title: POLAND: MERRILL SEES Q4 SLOWDOWN ON WARSAW BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: MERRILL SEES Q4 SLOWDOWN ON WARSAW BOURSE.

text.p: Price growth on the Warsaw Stock Exchange should slow over the fourth quarter after the bourse's surge thus far this year, Merrill Lynch said in its Third Quarter Review for European emerging markets.

"Following an impressive run in the year to date, many investors would undoubtedly welcome the opportunity to call it a year and return to the trampled search for value in January. Market momentum is expected to slow further in the fourth quarter," the report said.
The Warsaw bourse's main WIG index has risen 95 percent this year to 14,821.8 points.
Merrill said a good sign for the bourse was that the Polish economy remained sound and that any German economic revival should lift Polish exports.
It said direct investment was increasing as infrastructure development rose, with some construction stocks starting to benefit.
Merrill especially liked long-term infrastructure companies such as Elektrim , which it said had carved a niche position, as had food trader and producer Agros .

It said price-earnings ratios of blue-chip stocks in the high teens suggested more foreign playing but that a supply lack for the increasing foreign capital would last until copper firm KGHM and Bank Handlowy were floated in 1997's first half.
